chunks: Zurarah asked Abā Jaʿfar, peace be upon him, about a man who trims his nails, clips his mustache, and takes from the hair of his beard and his head: does that nullify the wudu (ablution)? So he said:
O Zurarah, all of this is sunnah (recommended practice), and wudu (ablution) is an obligation. Nothing from the sunnah invalidates the obligation, and indeed that increases it in purification.

key_terms.الْوُضُوءَ: wudu (ablution), the ritual state of purification for worship
key_terms.تَطْهِيرًا: an increase in purification and cleanliness
key_terms.سُنَّةٌ: a recommended prophetic practice, not an act that nullifies an obligation
key_terms.يَنْقُضُ: nullifies or breaks a ritual state

ai.seo_question: Do trimming nails, clipping the mustache, or cutting hair invalidate wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that trimming the nails, clipping the mustache, and taking hair from the beard or head do not nullify wudu (ablution). These acts are described as sunnah (recommended practice), while wudu is a binding obligation, and the former does not invalidate the latter; rather, such grooming increases purity.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.140 – Zurarah asked Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) about a man who trims his nails, clips his mustache, and cuts some of the hair from his beard and head. Does that nullify his ablution?

Imam (as) said: 'O’ Zurarah, all of this is Sunnah (recommended practice), while ablution is an obligation (fardh). None of the Sunnah practices invalidate an obligation. In fact, such practices increase one's purity.'.
